title: The Agentic AI Engineer - Benedikt Sanftl, Mutagent
talk_summary: The speakers describe an agentic AI engineer loop: spec-driven agent definition, eval-driven development with actionable/calibrated evals, production trace monitoring, failure-mode diagnosis, and optimization gated by evals. They demo an orchestrator plus evaluator/diagnostics agents that ingest traces and produce root-cause reports and markdown tasks for coding agents.

takeaways.technique: Binary actionable evals plus calibrated judge
takeaways.what_they_do: Build eval suites from metrics/criteria and datasets, prefer binary pass/fail criteria over score-based evals unless the rubric is very well defined, and calibrate LLM-as-judge to reduce run-to-run scoring noise.
takeaways.evidence_quote: using uh, binary type of evals or criteria, is preferred because there you have a kind of a call to action

takeaways.technique: Trace diagnostics to failure modes and new evals
takeaways.what_they_do: Run diagnostics over production traces: sample representative traces, identify frequent failure modes, group them by root cause, and produce remedies plus new eval criteria.
takeaways.evidence_quote: collect all the failures for your agents and do structured root cause analysis

takeaways.what_they_do: After initial deep trace reading, encode known failure modes as code-checkable indicators such as specific content or tool-call sequences, and use multi-tier filtering/segmentation to sample traces instead of LLM-reading all traces.

Write an agent spec covering responsibilities, context requirements, tools/integrations, jobs to be done and not done, and constraints; keep the spec separate from implementation so the harness or model can change.
takeaways.evidence_quote: spec is isolated from the implementation details

takeaways.what_they_do: Use the eval suite as a termination gate: agents can vary a feature or run experiments, and changes are automatically shipped only when evals are green.
takeaways.evidence_quote: as long as the eval suite is green then this again gets deployed to production

takeaways.technique: Orchestrator with trace/ticket connectors and task output
takeaways.what_they_do: An orchestrator dispatches evaluator/diagnostics subagents; connectors pull traces and incidents from observability, ticketing, and Slack; output is an HTML report and a markdown task definition for a coding agent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: orchestrator which kind of handles the dispatch for all the other sub agents or stages
